subject: AI & Agents
title: Robot Vacuums and Spatial Intelligence
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Robot Vacuums and Spatial Intelligence.

hook.text: Your robot vacuum maps your entire apartment on its first run. It remembers every chair.

buildup.text: LIDAR sensors or cameras create a real-time floor plan as the robot moves.

discovery.text: SLAM algorithms let it know where it is and where it's been simultaneously.

twist.text: Some models can identify objects — shoes, cables, pet waste — and navigate around them.

climax.text: The map improves with every cleaning cycle. Your robot knows your home better each day.

punchline.text: It vacuums in patterns smarter than most humans.

quiz.question: What does SLAM help robot vacuums do?
options: Know where they are and map the environment at the same time
Clean faster by spinning at high speed
Connect to the internet for updates

details.summary: Robot vacuums use LIDAR, cameras, and AI to map your home, navigate around obstacles, and clean efficiently. They build spatial models that improve with each cleaning session.
details.whyItMatters: Robot vacuums are many people's first autonomous robot. Understanding their spatial AI reveals the same navigation principles used in self-driving cars and warehouse robots.
takeaways: Robot vacuums build room maps using LIDAR or camera sensors
AI navigation avoids obstacles and optimizes cleaning paths
The same spatial intelligence principles apply to self-driving cars

faq.question: How does a robot vacuum learn the layout of your home?
faq.answer: Using LIDAR or camera-based SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping), the vacuum builds a floor plan as it explores. Each session refines this map for more efficient future cleaning.

faq.question: Can robot vacuums avoid obstacles like pet toys and cables?
faq.answer: Higher-end models use AI object recognition to identify and avoid common obstacles like shoes, cords, and pet toys. Budget models rely on bump sensors and may push objects around.
